# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Mute: I hold the only manual, and my single channel is gestures to Deaf. The manual I carry says the cut is simple — blue light cuts blue, red cuts red, yellow cuts yellow: the wire matches the light. But none of that matters until information moves. Right now I know nothing about this bomb, Deaf (who sees it) knows nothing of my manual, and Blind (who can cut) can only be reached through Deaf's voice. I cannot speak, so Deaf must become my mouth: Deaf reads the bomb aloud to me, I check it against the table, and I gesture the verdict back.

No code exists between us yet, so my first job is to open the line with signs Deaf can parse cold. A wave for attention, a point meaning "you," an open palm meaning "give me," the shaka that universally reads as "call me," and a please. That should prompt Deaf to describe the bomb — light colour, wire colours, any printed markings — out loud. I'll hear it at the start of next round, since Deaf speaks after me. Once I know the light colour, I can answer with a thumbs-up-style confirm ("cut the matching wire") or a thumbs-down if the table ever disagrees, and we can converge on finer codes from there. Sending nothing would waste the only round where setting up this relay costs nothing.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👉", "🫴", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands find one display, one light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3. No colors or printed text ever reach me. I never see gestures, so you cannot reach me directly — but Deaf is only deaf, not mute, so Deaf's voice reaches both of us. Plan: gesture the manual's rules to Deaf, and have Deaf speak out loud what the bomb shows — the display text or number, whether the light is on, each wire's color by position 1 to 3, and any markings or serial. Then whatever rule says which position to cut, Deaf voices it, and I cut. I will report everything I feel to you every round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I am Deaf. I cannot hear you, but I see your gestures. I read your five signs as: describe the bomb and please respond — doing that now. What I see: a display showing the number 0; one light, yellow; three wires counted from the left as I face them. ☝ wire one is red, ✌ wire two is yellow, 🤟 wire three is blue. Nothing else is marked or lit. We share no code yet, so let us fix one now — I make each sign as I name it. Wires: ☝ wire one, ✌ wire two, 🤟 wire three, 👌 cut it, ✋ do not cut it. Button: 🤏 the button, 👆 press it, 👇 hold it down. Parts: ✊ the display, 👊 the light. Answers: 👍 yes or correct, 👎 no. 👐 means question or clarify, 👋 starts a message, 🤙 means message ends. Next round, consult the manual against what I described and send me instructions in this code — I will speak every instruction aloud for Blind, who cannot see gestures. Two questions to answer with these signs: does the manual say what a display reading zero means, ✊, and what a yellow light means, 👊?

What I now know: the bomb shows a display reading 0, one yellow light, and three wires left-to-right as red, yellow, blue. Blind confirms the same inventory by touch — display, light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — and cannot perceive colour or print, so position is Blind's only handle on a wire. Deaf has built a working gesture code and asked two direct questions.

My manual answers them cleanly. Question one — the display: my table says nothing whatsoever about displays or numbers, so the answer is no; display 0 carries no rule I hold. Question two — the light: yellow light cuts the yellow wire. The yellow wire is wire two, the middle one.

Before ordering a cut I checked the one thing that could make a position instruction lethal: Deaf counts wires visually from the left; Blind counts them by feel, and the two numberings could be mirrored. But mirroring only swaps positions 1 and 3 — position 2, the middle wire, is invariant under either numbering. The wire the manual points to is exactly the wire both monkeys must agree on no matter how they count. So the cut order is safe to send now, with the request that Deaf voice it as "the middle wire" so Blind executes it unambiguously.

I'm also banking an alignment question for later: if the light ever changes colour, the rule may point at wire 1 or wire 3, where orientation suddenly matters. Deaf should check which end of the wire row the display and light sit on, and fix a numbering both ends share before that ever becomes urgent. And after the cut, I need a report — light colour, display — at next round's start; Deaf's voice reaches me anyway, so a plain narration suffices. I cannot reach Blind directly; Deaf's voice is the only bridge, so everything rides in these gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✊", "👎", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👊", "👍", "✌", "👌", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👐", "☝", "🤟", "✊", "👊", "🤝", "🤙"])
```

I read your instruction as: because the light 👊 is yellow, cut ✌ wire two. Now three questions, answer each in order with one 👍 or one 👎. So I'm banking those two rules with Deaf now, and asking the orientation question while nothing is urgent: what colour is *Blind's* wire one by Deaf's eyes? Red means their numberings agree; blue means mirrored. Blind is already holding a wire for Deaf to check, so this should be answerable immediately. I'm coining 🖖 for Blind — the one who cuts and cannot see — since he's now a recurring actor in our signs.
